translationRepairs.before: At that time Murong Wei succeeded to the false throne and Murong Ke was Grand Preceptor.
translationRepairs.after: At that time Murong Wei succeeded to the false throne and Murong Ke was Grand Steward.
translationRepairs.reason: 太宰 is Grand Steward, not Grand Preceptor; this is the parallel-field correction to the existing idiomatic proposal.

translationRepairs.before: Earlier, when Bao was at Chang'an, with Han Huang, Li Gen, and others he was at a banquet playing liubo; Bao sat upright and composed his appearance and swore, "The world says liubo has a god—is this empty talk!
translationRepairs.after: Earlier, when Bao was at Chang'an, he attended a banquet with Han Huang, Li Gen, and others and played chupu; Bao sat upright, composed his expression, and swore, "The world says chupu has a god—is this empty talk!
translationRepairs.reason: 摴蒱 is the game chupu, not liubo.

translationRepairs.before: Earlier, while Bao was at Chang'an, he played liubo at a feast with Han Huang, Li Gen, and others; sitting rigidly upright he swore, "Men say the dice have a god—surely that is no idle tale!
translationRepairs.after: Earlier, while Bao was at Chang'an, he played chupu at a feast with Han Huang, Li Gen, and others; sitting rigidly upright he swore, "Men say the gaming pieces have a god—surely that is no idle tale!
translationRepairs.reason: 摴蒱 is chupu; 五木 in s0075 confirms its five wooden gaming pieces, not liubo.

translationRepairs.before: His men are tired and few—strike now and take him."
translationRepairs.after: His generals are old and his soldiers weary—strike now and take him."
translationRepairs.reason: 將老兵疲 says the generals are old and the soldiers weary; it does not say the men are few.

translationRepairs.before: Chui refused, saying, "My father and I entrusted our lives to the Qin court; in peril we were saved, bearing the sovereign's unworldly grace and receiving the favor of renewed life—though called minister and ruler, our bond is as deep as father and son; how can we, for a small rift, harbor divided loyalties.
translationRepairs.after: Chui refused, saying, "My son and I entrusted our lives to the Qin court; in peril we were saved, bearing the sovereign's unworldly grace and receiving the favor of renewed life—though called minister and ruler, our bond is as deep as father and son; how can we, for a small rift, harbor divided loyalties.
translationRepairs.reason: 吾父子 means 'my son and I' here, not 'my father and I'; Chui and his son had taken refuge with Qin.

translationRepairs.before: Chui declined: "My father and I cast our lot with Qin in mortal danger and were spared; we owe the emperor a grace beyond measure and life itself—though called subject and lord, our bond is that of father and son; how could a small quarrel make us waver in loyalty?
translationRepairs.after: Chui declined: "My son and I cast our lot with Qin in mortal danger and were spared; we owe the emperor a grace beyond measure and life itself—though called subject and lord, our bond is that of father and son; how could a small quarrel make us waver in loyalty?
translationRepairs.reason: 吾父子 denotes Chui and his son, not Chui and his father.

translationRepairs.before: Chui led troops to Xingyang; in the eighth year of the Taiping reign of Emperor Xiaowu he styled himself Grand General, Grand Commander, and Prince of Yan, acting by imperial commission, and established the era name Yan Yuan.
translationRepairs.after: Chui led troops to Xingyang; in the eighth year of the Taiyuan era he styled himself Grand General, Grand Commander, and Prince of Yan, acting by imperial commission, and established the era name Yan Yuan.
translationRepairs.reason: 太元 is the Taiyuan era, not a Taiping reign.

translationRepairs.before: Chui said to Rang, "I received the sovereign's unworldly grace and therefore wished to keep the Marquis of Changle safe, have him send all his host to the capital, and then restore the house and state, remaining forever Qin's neighbor in good faith.
translationRepairs.after: Chui said to Rang, "I received the sovereign's unworldly grace and therefore wished to keep the Duke of Changle safe, have him send all his host to the capital, and then restore the house and state, remaining forever Qin's neighbor in good faith.
translationRepairs.reason: 長樂公 is Duke of Changle; this supplies the literal-field counterpart to the existing idiomatic proposal.

translationRepairs.before: The Princess of Changle is the sovereign's eldest son, his virtue surpassing Tang and Wei, holding the duty east of Shan—he is the court's bulwark; how can he meekly hand the general a hundred cities!
translationRepairs.after: The Duke of Changle is the sovereign's eldest son, his virtue surpassing Tang and Wei, holding the duty east of Shan—he is the court's bulwark; how can he meekly hand the general a hundred cities!
translationRepairs.reason: 長樂公 is Duke of Changle and 元子 explicitly says eldest son; 'Princess' contradicts both.

translationRepairs.before: Last summer Huan Chong came to his death; in one plan it was like clouds dispersed; returning to attack Xiangcheng, captives and severed ears numbered in the tens of thousands—this is truly Your Majesty's divine calculation, and also your foolish servant's effect of forgetting death.
translationRepairs.after: Last summer Huan Chong came courting death; at one stroke his forces dispersed like clouds; returning to attack Yuncheng, we took captives and severed ears by the tens of thousands—this was truly Your Majesty's divine calculation, and also the result of your foolish servant's disregard for death.
translationRepairs.reason: 送死 is hostile rhetoric for coming to court death, not a statement that Huan Chong died; 鄖城 is Yuncheng, not Xiangcheng, and 俘馘 distinguishes captives and severed ears.

translationRepairs.before: Last summer Huan Chong died; our plans cleared like clouds; at Xiangcheng we took tens of thousands of heads—this was your divine strategy and my small share of dying for you.
translationRepairs.after: Last summer Huan Chong came courting death; at one stroke his forces scattered like clouds; we then attacked Yuncheng and took tens of thousands of captives and severed ears—this was your divine strategy and my small share in risking death for you.
translationRepairs.reason: The sentence describes Huan Chong's failed attack, not his death; it names 鄖城 (Yuncheng) and 俘馘 (captives and severed ears), not Xiangcheng and heads alone.

translationRepairs.before: Your servant received the edict to tour the north and was constrained by the Marquis of Changle.
translationRepairs.after: Your servant received the edict to tour the north and was constrained by the Duke of Changle.
translationRepairs.reason: 長樂 refers to Fu Pi's title, Duke of Changle; this is the literal counterpart to the existing idiomatic proposal.

translationRepairs.before: When I reached Luoyang, the Plain Duke Hui again would not trust or accept me.
translationRepairs.after: When I reached Luoyang, Fu Hui, Duke of Pingyuan, again would not trust or accept me.
translationRepairs.reason: 平原公暉 is Fu Hui with the fief title Duke of Pingyuan, not a 'Plain Duke'; this parallels the existing idiomatic proposal.

translationRepairs.before: I wished to have the Marquis of Changle send all his host to the rescue and dismiss them with ceremony, but Pi obstinately held the will of a common man and did not comprehend the principle of change.
translationRepairs.after: I wished to have the Duke of Changle send all his host to the rescue and dismiss them with ceremony, but Pi obstinately held the will of a common man and did not comprehend the principle of change.
translationRepairs.reason: 長樂公 is Duke of Changle; this is the literal counterpart to the existing idiomatic proposal.

translationRepairs.before: We were about to entrust you with the office of chief minister and enfeoff you as marquis of a commandery, hoping broadly to cross hardship and respectfully repay your merit—why has Bo Yi suddenly destroyed his icy integrity and willow Hui instantly become a debauched man!
translationRepairs.after: We were about to entrust you with the office of chief minister and enfeoff you as marquis of a commandery, hoping broadly to cross hardship and respectfully repay your merit—why has Bo Yi suddenly destroyed his icy integrity and Liuxia Hui instantly become a debauched man!
translationRepairs.reason: 柳惠 is the abbreviated name of the exemplar Liuxia Hui, not the phrase 'willow Hui'.

translationRepairs.before: I would have made you chief minister and marquis of a commandery to repay your merit—why has Bo Yi shattered his honor and Liu Hui turned debauched!
translationRepairs.after: I would have made you chief minister and marquis of a commandery to repay your merit—why has Bo Yi shattered his honor and Liuxia Hui turned debauched!
translationRepairs.reason: 柳惠 refers to Liuxia Hui; the extraction itself canonically identifies p070 as Liuxia Hui.

translationRepairs.before: Only the Marquis of Changle and the Plain Duke, in years not yet established, met you in the Two Capitals—we regret that their planning and conduct did not match Our heart; this is the only thing regretted."
translationRepairs.after: Only the Duke of Changle and the Duke of Pingyuan, in years not yet established, met you in the Two Capitals—we regret that their planning and conduct did not match Our heart; this is the only thing regretted."
translationRepairs.reason: 長樂 and 平原 are the fief titles Duke of Changle and Duke of Pingyuan; this is the literal counterpart to existing title repairs.

translationRepairs.before: Bin's nephew Zhen fled north to Handan and marched on Ye to join Pi from within; Chui sent Bao and Murong Long to break him.
translationRepairs.after: Bin's nephew Zhen fled north to Handan and marched on Ye, intending to coordinate with Pi from outside and inside; Chui sent Bao and Murong Long to break him.
translationRepairs.reason: 欲與丕為內外之勢 means Zhen outside and Fu Pi inside would form a coordinated external-internal position; Zhen was not joining Pi 'from within'.

translationRepairs.before: Chui himself fled north from Xincheng; Laozhi pursued Chui and in successive battles all were defeats.
translationRepairs.after: Chui fled north from Xincheng; Laozhi pursued him but was defeated in every successive battle.
translationRepairs.reason: 牢之 is the subject of 追 and remains the subject of 連戰皆敗; s0206 immediately continues with the Jin royal army's defeat.

translationRepairs.before: Chui fled north; Laozhi pursued and defeated him again and again.
translationRepairs.after: Chui fled north; Laozhi pursued but was defeated again and again.
translationRepairs.reason: The idiomatic translation reverses the outcome: 連戰皆敗 says Liu Laozhi lost the successive engagements.

translationRepairs.before: The General Who Establishes the Commandery Xu Yan rebelled at Wuyi, drove and plundered more than four thousand men, and fled north to Youzhou.
translationRepairs.after: The General Who Establishes the Standard Xu Yan rebelled at Wuyi, drove off and plundered more than four thousand people, and fled north to Youzhou.
translationRepairs.reason: 建節 is an official title involving the command standard 節, not a commandery.

translationRepairs.before: Liao in terror sued for peace.
translationRepairs.after: Liao in terror sent an envoy to request surrender.
translationRepairs.reason: 遣使請降 explicitly says he sent an envoy to ask to surrender, not merely to seek peace.

translationRepairs.before: Yong thought Chui was using a deceptive route to attack him and therefore gathered all his armies back to guard the Zhatai Pass at Huatai.
translationRepairs.after: Yong thought Chui was attacking him by a deceptive route and therefore gathered all his armies back to guard the Taihang and Zhi passes.
translationRepairs.reason: 太行軹關 names the Taihang passes and Zhi Pass, not a 'Zhatai Pass at Huatai'; this supplies the literal counterpart to the existing idiomatic proposal.

translationRepairs.before: Chui advanced the army entering from Tianjing Pass, reaching Hubei.
translationRepairs.after: Chui advanced the army through Tianjing Pass and reached Hubi.
translationRepairs.reason: 壺壁 is the place Hubi, not Hubei.

translationRepairs.before: Chui entered by Tianjing Pass and reached Hubei.
translationRepairs.after: Chui entered by Tianjing Pass and reached Hubi.
translationRepairs.reason: 壺壁 is Hubi; s0258 repeats the same place.

translationRepairs.before: Chui, ashamed and indignant, spat blood; because of this he took to his bed ill, riding in a litter he advanced.
translationRepairs.after: Chui, ashamed and indignant, vomited blood; because of this he fell ill and advanced in a horse-drawn litter.
translationRepairs.reason: 歐血 (嘔血) means vomited blood; 馬輿 is a horse-drawn carriage or litter, not an assertion that he rode while bedridden.

translationRepairs.before: Chui, shamed and raging, coughed blood, fell ill, and was carried forward in a litter.
translationRepairs.after: Chui, shamed and raging, vomited blood, fell ill, and was carried forward in a horse-drawn litter.
translationRepairs.reason: 歐血 (嘔血) is vomiting blood, not coughing blood.

translationRepairs.before: Bao and the rest, reaching Yunzhong, heard Chui was dying and turned back.
translationRepairs.after: Bao and the rest, reaching Yunzhong, heard Chui was ill and turned back.
translationRepairs.reason: 聞垂疾 says they heard of Chui's illness; it does not say he was dying.

translationRepairs.before: Taking his Left Chief Clerk Guan Wei of Ku Ruo, Right Chief Clerk Duan Chong, and Dragon-Charger Zhang Chong, together with the Administrator of Zhongshan Feng Heng, as Minister of the Imperial Secretariat; Murong De as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Commander of All Armies Within and Without, and Colonel Director of Convicts; the Pacifying General Murong Lin as Guards Grand General; the rest received appointments according to rank.
translationRepairs.after: He appointed Kuruguan Wei Left Chief Clerk, Duan Chong Right Chief Clerk, and Zhang Chong Dragon-Prancing General; he made Feng Heng, Administrator of Zhongshan, Minister of Personnel; Murong De Palace Attendant, Commander of All Armies Within and Without, and concurrently Colonel-Director of Retainers; and the Pacifying General Murong Lin Grand General of the Guards. The rest received appointments according to rank.
translationRepairs.reason: 庫辱官 is Kuruguan's compound surname; only 中山尹封衡 is made 吏部尚書, and 司隸校尉 is Colonel-Director of Retainers. The current grouping wrongly makes all four men one minister.

translationRepairs.before: He appointed his left chief clerk Guan Wei of Ku Ruo, right chief clerk Duan Chong, dragon-cavalry commander Zhang Chong, and the governor of Zhongshan Feng Heng as Minister of the Civil Office; Murong De as Attendant-in-Ordinary, commander of all armies inside and outside the realm, and colonel of the masters of writing; the Pacifying General Murong Lin as Grand General of the Guards; and the remainder received posts according to merit.
translationRepairs.after: He appointed Kuruguan Wei Left Chief Clerk, Duan Chong Right Chief Clerk, and Zhang Chong Dragon-Prancing General; he made Feng Heng, Governor of Zhongshan, Minister of Personnel; Murong De Palace Attendant, Commander of All Armies Inside and Outside, and concurrently Colonel-Director of Retainers; and the Pacifying General Murong Lin Grand General of the Guards. The rest received posts by rank.
translationRepairs.reason: The existing proposal correctly fixes Kuruguan and 司隸校尉 but still misgroups all four preceding men as Minister of Personnel; the Chinese assigns 吏部尚書 to Feng Heng alone.

translationRepairs.before: The Erudites Liu Xiang and Dong Mi argued that Yao's mother held the third rank among consorts, that the honored tomb was not Jiang Yuan's, making clear that the way of sage-kings put supreme impartiality first.
translationRepairs.after: The Erudites Liu Xiang and Dong Mi argued that Yao's mother occupied the third rank among the consorts and did not use her honored status to outrank Jiang Yuan, showing that the way of sage-kings puts perfect impartiality first.
translationRepairs.reason: 不以貴陵薑嫄 means she did not rely on honored status to overtop Jiang Yuan; 陵 is a verb here, not a tomb.

translationRepairs.before: The erudites Liu Xiang and Dong Mi argued that the mother of Yao ranked only third among consorts and that the honored tomb was not that of Jiang Yuan, showing that the way of sage-kings put supreme impartiality above birth and rank.
translationRepairs.after: The erudites Liu Xiang and Dong Mi argued that Yao's mother ranked only third among the consorts and did not use her honored status to outrank Jiang Yuan, showing that the way of sage-kings put perfect impartiality first.
translationRepairs.reason: 陵 is verbal ('overstep/outrank'), so the clause is not about an honored tomb.

extractionIssues.detail: The extraction splits clearly continuous same-chapter people into duplicate IDs: Murong Chui p001/p029/p057/p092/p129; Fu Jian p013/p028/p058/p114; Fu Pi p038/p060/p093; Murong Bao p016/p055/p075/p096/p141; Murong De p018/p054/p079/p101/p131; Murong Wei p008/p043/p080/p123; Murong Nong p045/p067/p094/p138; Murong Kai p046/p077/p111/p137; Murong Shao p047/p112/p143; Murong Long p076/p122/p146; Han Xin p025/p031/p063; Fu Hui p039/p062; Fu Feilong p041/p061; Shi Yue p036/p068; Zhai Bin p040/p071; Kuruguan Wei p051/p097; Murong Zhou p048/p113; Feng Heng p072/p100; Zhai Liao p085/p119; Xu Yan p088/p095; Murong Huang p002/p104; Murong Lin p102/p142; Murong Guo p128/p139; and Zhang Chong p099/p133.
extractionIssues.proposedFix: Merge each listed same-person group and repoint all surfaces, claims, relationships, and chronology to the retained chapter-local person ID. Do not include p120 in the Murong Ke merge until its unsupported identification is resolved.

extractionIssues.detail: p120 is named 'Murong Ke' and p111 (Murong Kai) is asserted to be his son, but s0221 supplies only the title 太原王; this chapter never names that referent as Murong Ke. The source-form title does not support silently manufacturing the personal name.
extractionIssues.proposedFix: Retain the source-form referent 'Prince of Taiyuan' as unresolved, or link it only after independent evidence establishes the identity; remove the p111→p120 parent claim unless that identification is separately supported.

extractionIssues.detail: The extraction says Huan Chong 'died last summer' and labels the attestation event his death. 送死 here says he came courting death in a failed attack; it does not report his death.
extractionIssues.proposedFix: Delete the death claim and describe the event as Huan Chong's failed attack followed by the attack on Yuncheng.

extractionIssues.detail: Liu Laozhi's event claim says he defeated Chui and then was routed only at Wuqiao. It omits and conflicts with s0205, where Laozhi pursued Chui but lost every successive engagement.
extractionIssues.proposedFix: Record that Laozhi defeated Chui at Ye in s0204, then lost the successive pursuit battles in s0205 and was defeated again at Wuqiao in s0206.

extractionIssues.detail: The claim renders 建節將軍 as 'General Who Establishes Integrity'; the current literal translation instead incorrectly says 'Commandery'. 節 is the command standard/tally in this title.
extractionIssues.proposedFix: Normalize the English office label to 'General Who Establishes the Standard' (or the project's established equivalent for 建節將軍) while retaining the exact Chinese.

extractionIssues.detail: The canonical record correctly identifies Liuxia Hui, but its captured English surface is 'Liu Hui', inherited from the defective translation.
extractionIssues.proposedFix: After the translation repair, replace the English mention surface with 'Liuxia Hui'; retain 柳惠 as the exact Chinese abbreviated form.

extractionIssues.detail: The canonical record correctly has Kuruguan Wei, but its English mention surface is 'Guan Wei', inherited from parsing the compound surname 庫辱官 as a place.
extractionIssues.proposedFix: Replace the English mention surface with 'Kuruguan Wei' after the translation repair.

extractionIssues.detail: The event claim says Zhai Liao 'sued for peace'; 請降 says he requested surrender, followed by bare-chested submission.
extractionIssues.proposedFix: Change the event action to 'sent an envoy to request surrender and then submitted bare-chested'.

extractionIssues.detail: Zhai Zhao is said to take his wife and children (攜妻子) when he flees, but his extraction has no family-summary claim for them.
extractionIssues.proposedFix: Add an explicit family-summary for an unnamed wife and children, without inventing names, counts, or identities.

chronologyNotes.detail: The existing date audit is stale. The extraction contains many asserted Western years and intervals, while the chapter usually gives events, relative sequence, or regnal years. Preserve the Chinese date witnesses and require a fresh independent audit; this review does not approve any Western conversion.
The asserted AD 384 'death of Huan Chong' is doubly unsupported: 去夏 is only a relative 'last summer', and 送死 does not say Huan Chong died. Remove the death event and re-audit any year separately.

The extraction assigns AD 394 to the Changzi campaign from the witness 於是議征長子, which contains no year or era. AD 394 may be externally recoverable, but it is unsupported by this chapter text alone and must not pass while the date audit is stale.
The extraction assigns AD 395 to the Canhe campaign from the place/event name 參合, not from an expressed date. That Western year needs independent evidence.

These units do provide regnal witnesses 太元八年, 太元十一年, and 太元二十一年. The extraction converts them to AD 383, AD 386, and AD 396; retain the regnal dates, but treat the Western mappings as pending fresh date review rather than approved.

summary: Reviewed all 298 units and both English fields, plus all 14 existing proposed repairs. Found 32 additional or refined field-level repairs across 23 units; together with the existing proposals, 27 units have definite translation defects and 271 have no definite translation defect found. The most consequential findings are the reversed battle outcome in s0205, the false Huan Chong death in s0148, 'my father and I' for 吾父子 in s0102, the still-misgrouped s0295 existing proposal, and the extraction's extensive duplicate splitting of continuous people. Nine clear extraction issues and five chronology cautions are recorded; no Western year is approved.
